page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2700.18. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25% at the same score, reflecting the physical core limitation. Memory bandwidth is generally constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 128.68 GB/sec, and large block read/write speeds landing in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while complex multi-core workloads, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, score in the bottom 10% to 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2as_v5 offers a low-entry hardware profile with dedicated CPU allocation, making it a viable option for lightweight workloads that require consistent CPU access without the credit-depletion risks of burstable instances. Given the poor multi-core and database benchmark results, it is not suited for heavy database operations or parallelized build pipelines. Instead, it is best aligned with basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, lightweight text processing, and small-scale application hosting.
